title: Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, probes continue
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: CNBC reports Nvidia fell about 8% on Wed 25 Nov after a 5.9% drop Tuesday, according to GuruFocus, as the rally after Huang's return faded on worries about AI spending, tariffs and rates; Bloomberg reports the stock is still 35% below its 6 Oct peak and says the California probe continues. The board committee's investigation is still open, and Investing.com reports Huang faces closed-door House interviews on 1 Dec and a Senate Banking hearing on 3 Dec.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
next_label: House committees' closed-door interview with Huang, Senate hearing 3 Dec
sources: Nvidia, CNBC, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance, GuruFocus, CNN, Al Jazeera, Investing.com

title: US proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 others
since_label: Tue 24 Nov 13:00 UTC, before the WSJ tariff report
status: Axios, CNBC and the Washington Post report that on Wed 25 Nov USTR Greer proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including an extra 20% on most Chinese imports and 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland; CNBC reports chipmakers led a sell-off that took the Nasdaq Composite down nearly 4%. The proposal now goes to public comment and hearings, and Greer told CNBC the tariffs likely will not take effect for months, while Axios cites an official saying China's rate could rise to 40% if talks break down.
why: Tariffs on China and the EU hit chip and AI hardware supply chains and feed inflation and Fed hike odds, which weigh on the Nasdaq and crypto together.
next_label: Public comment and hearings, not in force before January per a US official
sources: USTR, WSJ, Axios, CNBC, Washington Post, Yahoo Finance, The Hill, Bloomberg

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Benzinga reports bitcoin fell 3.6% to about $57,862 by late morning Wed 25 Nov, and Bitcoin Magazine reports Strategy fell about 8% to near $71 in early trading after an 8.1% drop Tuesday. Crypto.news reports Strategy spent $211.8M buying back its STRC preferred shares last week against $29.6M on bitcoin; MSCI's deletion takes effect after the 30 Nov close, and it is still open whether other index providers will follow.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Benzinga, Bitcoin Magazine, crypto.news, TradingNews, Investing News

title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: Investing.com reports ANT closed Tue 24 Nov at $81.91, below its $83 IPO price, and Google Finance data show it hit a new low of $73.85 on Wed 25 Nov before trading near $79.60. CNBC reports analysts are still largely positive; whether ANT gets back above its IPO price and when it joins the Nasdaq 100 are still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
sources: CNBC, Investing.com, Google Finance, StockAnalysis, Quartz, Fast Company, Bloomberg

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: Reuters reports Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more tankers hit naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz on Wed 25 Nov, and Fars reported a third; HNGN reports Saudi air defenses shot down drones over the Ras Tanura oil terminal. Tehran has tied reopening the strait to lifting the US naval blockade, and no ceasefire has been announced.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: Reuters, Arab News, OilPrice, CNBC, Anadolu, HNGN, Tehran Times, CoinDesk
